items.title: The CLI reaches core over MCP JSON-RPC, and that is what pins 60 tools in place
items.description:
## What happens today

Every one of the CLI's 21 verbs reaches core through a single function, `rpc("tools/call", …)` in `src/tracker/rpc.mjs`, which speaks MCP JSON-RPC to `<core>/mcp`. The REST API that core presents as its main contract is not touched by this CLI at all.

## Outcome

`forge` reaches core over the REST API. MCP stops being this plugin's transport.

## Why this is critical rather than a cleanup

Core's MCP surface is 60 registered tools, and the decision to shrink it to the session-lifecycle group is already taken and half-executed: three waves shipped and deleted 10 tools.

The next wave cannot start, because 7 of the tools it would delete are the ones this CLI calls:

```
forge_issues   forge_comments   forge_config   forge_guide
forge_knowledge   forge_project_pm   forge_projects.create
```

**This CLI is the single reason that surface cannot shrink.** Nothing else on a runner box calls those tools.

## Business rules

- **Same 21 verbs, same output shapes.** This is a transport change, not a redesign. A verb that behaves differently after the move is a regression, not an improvement.
- **Credential is the job-scoped PAT.** The agent process is given `$FORGE_PAT`, `$FORGE_PROJECT_ID` and `$FORGE_PROJECT_SLUG` and nothing else — no run id, no job id, no session id. Every project-scoped route takes the project **UUID** as a path segment; only `/mcp` resolves `X-Forge-Project-Slug`. So paths are built from the id, and a verb that only knows a slug resolves the id first.
- **Two tools do not move and must keep an MCP path.** `forge_uploads` returns an image content block to a multimodal model, which a shell process cannot produce. `forge_step_start` opens the session every other call reports into and hands back the issue body the runner did not inline. Anything routing through those stays as it is.
- **The PAT fence is an allowlist, not a deny-list.** 16 prefixes. A route not on it answers `403 PAT_NOT_PERMITTED`. That is a gap to report to the forge repo by name — never a reason to fall back to MCP silently, because a silent fallback is what makes the tool undeletable again.
- **`forge call`, `forge tools`, `forge schema` are MCP-shaped verbs.** Decide what each means once the transport is REST, and say so in the help text. Leaving one half-working is worse than removing it: the CLI's own help is the contract an agent reads.

## Invariant

A verb that cannot be served over REST **fails loudly naming the route it wanted**. It does not quietly keep using MCP. A partial migration that still holds one tool open has delivered nothing, because the deletion wave is all-or-nothing per tool.

## Out of scope

Deleting any tool on core. That is the forge repo's work and it waits on this.

## The map

`docs/architecture/data-plane-surface.md` in the forge repo lists the REST twin for every tool, verified 2026-09-01 against `registered-tools.ts`, the mounts in `index.ts`, and `PAT_ALLOWED_PREFIXES`. Each row was checked to call the same service as the tool, not merely to carry a similar name. Read it before deriving anything.

## Ordering

The forge repo carries the matching issue for the deletions. It is blocked by this one. A cross-project dependency edge could not be recorded, so the constraint lives here in prose: **nothing on core is deleted until this ships.**
items.plan:
# ISS-508 — the CLI reaches core over REST, and one declared table says how

Screen change: no
Schema coupling: no
User-facing outcome: yes

## The one thing verified in code that makes this possible

`plugin/src/resolve/settings.mjs:110` already sends `Bearer <token>`, and the token in
`~/.config/forge/config.json` is a personal access token (`forge_pat_…`). Every route this change
needs was called with exactly that credential against `https://forge-beta-api.sidcorp.co` during
planning and answered 200 — including the two writes, `PATCH /api/issues/:id` and
`POST /api/issues/:id/comments`, each read back and each rolled back. Nothing here rests on a
credential the run does not hold.

Two derivations the map did not carry, both proven rather than reasoned:

- `relations.blocks` / `relations.blockedBy` is `GET /api/issues/:id/dependencies`'s
  `outgoing` / `incoming`. Compared field for field on ISS-516: `edgeId`=`id`,
  `otherIssueId`/`otherDisplayId`/`otherStatus`/`otherMergedAt` are the `to*` columns on an
  outgoing edge and the `from*` columns on an incoming one, and `expired` is
  `validUntil !== null && validUntil < now`. So `forge_issues` can move whole.
- `filters.search` has no query parameter on the list route — `search=zzzznomatchzzz` still
  answered `total=516` — and is `GET /api/projects/:id/issues/search?q=`, a route of its own.

## What happens today

`plugin/src/tracker/rpc.mjs` has one exit, `rpc("tools/call", …)` to `<url>/mcp`, and three seams
every other module calls: `scoped`, `write`, `tried`. `aimed()` decides whether to send `projectId`
by reading the MCP tool declaration; `enumAt` reads `--fields` narrowing out of the same
declaration; `documentIdOf` bisects on `createdBefore`/`createdAfter` because MCP offers no cursor;
`unfencedIn` strips the tracker's untrusted-data marker off `structuredContent`, which ISS-458 made
this module's one home.

## What happens after

One declared table in a new `plugin/src/tracker/rest.mjs`, keyed `(tool, action)`, each row naming
its method, its path template, which segment carries the project id, the request the CLI sends and
the projection that turns the answer back into the shape the tool answered with. `scoped`, `write`
and `tried` read that table; every call site above them keeps its `(tool, action, args)` argument
form byte for byte, so no verb's output shape moves.

Rows, all proven live during planning:

| tool.action | route |
|---|---|
| `forge_issues.list` | `GET /projects/:project/issues` (+`/search?q=` when `filters.search` is set) |
| `forge_issues.get` | `GET /issues/:documentId`, plus `GET /issues/:documentId/dependencies` for `relations` |
| `forge_issues.create` | `POST /projects/:project/issues` |
| `forge_issues.update` | `PATCH /issues/:documentId` |
| `forge_issues.transition` | `POST /issues/:documentId/transition` (`toStatus`) |
| `forge_issues.mark_merged` | `POST /issues/:documentId/merge` |
| `forge_comments.list` / `.create` | `GET` / `POST /issues/:issue/comments` |
| `forge_knowledge.get` | `GET /projects/:project/knowledge/:slug` |
| `forge_knowledge.list` | `GET /projects/:project/knowledge` |
| `forge_knowledge.upsert` | `PUT /projects/:project/knowledge/:slug` |
| `forge_knowledge.delete` | `DELETE /projects/:project/knowledge/:slug` |
| `forge_memory.search` | `POST /memory/search` |
| `forge_config.get` | `GET /projects/:project/pipeline-config` |
| `forge_guide.list` / `.get` | `GET /guides`, `GET /guides/:slug` |
| `forge_projects.list` / `.get` | `GET /projects`, `GET /projects/:project` |
| `forge_project_pm.snapshot` / `.graph` / `.runner_load` | `GET /projects/:project/pm/{snapshot,graph,runner-load}` |
| `forge_uploads.*` | **stays on `/mcp`**, declared in the table as such |
| `forge_step_start` | **stays on `/mcp`**, declared in the table as such |

The REST base is derived from the one configured url by replacing its trailing `/mcp` with `/api`;
there is no second setting, and `forge doctor` prints both forms off that one value.

**Four things move with the transport, each because its old source disappears:**

1. `aimed()` stops reading a tool declaration. Whether a call is project-scoped is the table row's
   `:project` segment.
2. `--fields` loses its server-side narrowing path. The list and get routes serve whole rows and
   accept no `fields`/`view` parameter (probed: 35 keys either way), so `projectedTo` in
   `issues.mjs` becomes the only path and `FIELDS_AT` goes with `tools/list`.

   **`enumAt` is replaced rather than retired, and so is the misplaced-argument diagnostic.**
   `plugin/src/tools/knowledge.mjs:52` reads the tool's own enum to refuse a bad `kind`,
   `injection`, `confidence` or `authoredBy` before the write, and the REST routes answer a bare
   `{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"invalid body"}` with no allowed set (probed on the list route
   and twice on the upsert), so letting the tracker refuse would leave a message a developer cannot
   act on. The table therefore carries a `declares` column holding those sets, and the refusal says
   they are this CLI's declaration and go stale when the tracker grows a value — which is what the
   comment above `checked` currently denies and this change rewrites.

   `misplaced()` in `rpc.mjs`, which reads `toolNamed(name)?.inputSchema` to say where a rejected key
   really lives, is replaced by rendering the tracker's own validation error: the issue routes carry
   `details.formErrors` and `details.fieldErrors` naming the unrecognized key and, for an enum, the
   values it accepts (probed: `Unrecognized key: "status"`, and the full status enum on a bad
   `status`). `readable()` grows that shape and drops the schema walk; `keyPaths` and
   `REFERENCE_KEYS` go with it.
3. `documentIdOf` stops bisecting. The list envelope carries `offset` and `total`, so the walk pages
   by offset; `createdBefore`/`createdAfter` have no REST parameter and their windowing goes.
4. `unfencedIn` runs over every decoded REST body, keeping this module the marker's one home
   (ISS-458). The REST path would otherwise skip it and move that home without anyone deciding.

`retryOf` is re-derived from the table rather than from `arguments.action`: a row's method decides,
`GET` being repeatable and everything else not, and the `AMBIGUOUS` sentence about the merged mark
stays attached to the non-repeatable case.

**The two soft paths stay two.** `callTool`'s `soft` hands back the tool's own refusal and
`rpc`'s hands back a transport failure, and a caller beside its real work needs the second so
`fail()` does not exit past it. Under REST a 4xx carrying the tracker's own `{code, message}` is
the first and a dropped socket, a 5xx or an unparseable body is the second; the table does not
collapse them.

**`forge knowledge search` has no route and refuses.** Six candidate paths were probed and every one
404s (`/api/knowledge`, `/api/knowledge/search` on both methods, `/api/projects/:id/knowledge/search`
on both, `?q=`/`?search=` on the list route, which answered the same 16 rows either way);
`GET /api/projects/:id/knowledge/search` answers *knowledge entry not found*, so that path is
shadowed by the `/:slug` handler and no search route can live there. Per the issue's invariant the
verb fails loudly naming `POST /api/projects/:id/knowledge/search` as the route it wanted, and names
`forge knowledge list` and `forge knowledge get <slug>` as what still serves. The gap is filed
against the forge repo's own project, `forge-dev`.

**The three MCP-shaped verbs are decided, not left half-working:**

- `forge tools` prints the route table — one row per `(tool, action)` with its method and path, and
  the `forge_uploads` rows marked as the MCP ones. The withhold list in `config.json` keeps working
  because it is keyed by tool name, which the table's rows still carry, and `--all` still looks past
  it.
- `forge schema <tool>` prints that tool's rows: the arguments this CLI sends per action and the
  fields its projection answers with. It stops printing the tracker's MCP declaration, because that
  declaration is what this change exists to let core delete. Its help says so and points at
  `forge guide` for the tracker's own field documentation.
- `forge call <tool> '<json>'` keeps its argument form and goes through the table. A tool or action
  with no row fails naming the unsupported `(tool, action)` pair and pointing at `forge tools`,
  because an arbitrary name has no route to want and inventing one would be a misleading message.
  Naming the route it wanted is reserved for a capability this CLI declares and REST does not
  serve, which today is `forge_knowledge.search` alone. Neither case falls back to `/mcp`.

## Files

- `plugin/src/tracker/rest.mjs` — new: the table, the path builder, the projections, the caller.
- `plugin/src/tracker/rpc.mjs` — `scoped`/`write`/`tried`/`callTool` route through the table;
  `post` keeps the `/mcp` body for the rows declared MCP; `retryOf` re-derived; `unfencedIn` over
  every REST body; `aimed`/`enumAt`/`tools`/`toolNamed` and the tools cache retired or narrowed to
  the MCP rows.
- `plugin/src/tracker/issues.mjs` — the offset walk; `projectedTo` as the only `--fields` path.
- `plugin/src/tools/knowledge.mjs` — the search refusal.
- `plugin/src/commands.mjs` — `tools`, `schema`, `call` against the table.
- `plugin/src/tools/doctor.mjs` — both endpoint forms; the capability probe over the table's rows.
- `plugin/src/tracker/project-config.mjs`, `plugin/src/tracker/comments.mjs`,
  `plugin/src/tracker/field-write.mjs`, `plugin/src/tracker/filing/neighbours.mjs`,
  `plugin/src/tracker/filing/route.mjs`, `plugin/src/tracker/filing/landed.mjs`,
  `plugin/src/tracker/evidence.mjs`, `plugin/src/flow/advance.mjs`, `plugin/src/flow/record.mjs`,
  `plugin/src/flow/claim.mjs`, `plugin/src/flow/lease.mjs`, `plugin/src/rank/next.mjs`,
  `plugin/src/tools/deps.mjs` — only where a shape, an action name or an envelope key has to change.
- `plugin/test/fixtures.mjs` — `fakeTracker` becomes a REST router. `state.answer[<tool name>]` stays
  the authoring interface, so a test that asserts on the answer rather than on the wire is untouched;
  the fixture owns the inverse, tool-answer to REST envelope.
- `plugin/test/tracker/issue-fields.test.mjs` — the exception to that. It asserts on the wire:
  `args.fields` equals `[["plan"]]` and a declaration-only name narrows. Those are the route this
  change removes, so the assertions become body-projection ones rather than being kept alive on a
  synthetic argument, which would hide the behaviour change instead of proving it. The `Proof` lines
  of `AC-02-1-4`, `AC-02-1-6` and `AC-02-1-7` follow whatever the case names become.
- `plugin/test/tracker/rest.test.mjs` and `plugin/test/fixtures/rest/*.json` — new: the projections
  pinned against REST bodies captured live during planning and checked in, so a fixture and a
  transport that are mirrored-wrong cannot both be green.
- `docs/cli/one-transport.md` (cited in `rpc.mjs`'s own header), `docs/cli/beside.md` (its whole
  subject is the MCP dotted-action reading), `docs/cli/the-projections.md`, `docs/FORGE-CLI.md`,
  `plugin/skills/forge/SKILL.md`, `plugin/guides/skills/forge/references/configuration.md`,
  `plugin/guides/issue-flow-contract.md`, `README.md`.

- `docs/requirements/srs/19-external-interfaces.md` — EI-01 and its first acceptance criterion.
- `docs/requirements/srs/fr-02-tracker-surface.md` — UC-02-1, three of its criteria, and UC-02-6.
- `docs/requirements/srs/02-system-overview.md` — the CLI row's single-request-per-call sentence.

## The requirements clauses this revises

`EI-01` describes one request per call over the tracker's own endpoint with the project's slug in
the request, and its `AC-19-1-1` obliges the CLI to read the tracker's declared surface rather than
assume it. Both are exactly what this change reverses: the project travels as a path segment
carrying its uuid, and the CLI declares the surface itself because the declaration it used to read
is what core is about to delete. Both move to revision 2 in this change, the criteria cite them at
that revision, and the acceptance criterion's `Proof` names the new
`plugin/test/tracker/rest.test.mjs`. `EI-01`'s ownership sentences and `AC-19-1-2`'s data-fence
guarantee survive unchanged and are carried into revision 2 as they stand.

`UC-02-1` says a field may be asked for *whether or not the tracker will project that field itself*,
and three of its criteria are built on the two routes that reading gives:

- `AC-02-1-5`, the wire-narrowing route, is **retired** — the REST read routes accept no field
  parameter, so the route it obliges no longer exists.
- `AC-02-1-6` refuses a name *neither the tracker declares nor the body carries*; at revision 2 the
  body alone decides.
- `AC-02-1-7` obliges one read *whichever of the two routes* the names take; at revision 2 there is
  one route.

`UC-02-1` itself moves to revision 3, dropping the sentence about the tracker's own projection.

`UC-02-6` promises that a verb the CLI does not wrap is still callable with its own payload. A
closed route table makes that false for an action no row names, so it moves to revision 2 scoping
the promise to the capabilities the CLI declares, with the refusal for the rest named as the way
this is found out rather than left to be discovered.

`02-system-overview.md`'s CLI row says the tracker is reached over a single request per call, and
the issue read now composes two. That sentence moves with `EI-01`, because a tree whose overview
contradicts its interface clause is one where neither can be trusted.

## The documented convention this reverses

`plugin/guides/issue-flow-contract.md:716` states **The schema is the document** — that
`forge schema forge_issues` carries the tracker's entry criteria in the tool's own words. Once core
deletes the tool that declaration is gone, so the same change rewrites that line to name
`forge advance --owed` and `forge guide contract <status>` as the sources, and `forge schema` as what
this CLI sends.

## What this deliberately does not change

- No tool is deleted on core. That is the forge repo's work and it waits on this.
- `forge_uploads` and `forge_step_start` keep their MCP path, by the issue's own rule.
- No verb's arguments, output shape, refusal wording or exit code changes, except the three named
  above and `forge knowledge search`.
- `plugin/src/stats/`, `tools/run.mjs`, `tools/run/lock.mjs`, `plugin/guides/skills/dispatch/`,
  `docs/requirements/srs/fr-08-irreversible-commands.md` and `docs/requirements/README.md` are held
  by other runs in this wave and are not touched; a finding for any of them is routed with
  `forge new --into`.
- The `sessionContext` lease semantics, the fold floors, the ladder and the duplicate check keep
  their current behaviour; only the calls under them change transport.

## The way back

One `git revert` of the ship commit and a second ship. Every step is a source edit and the plugin
cache copy is written per version, so nothing outside the checkout has to be undone. Reversing one
table row is what undoes any single route decision, including the knowledge-search refusal.
items.acceptanceCriteria:

3. `forge issue ISS-508 --full` prints the same top-level field names it printed at d0e4784, judged against output captured at d0e4784 and attached.
4. `forge issue ISS-516 --fields relations` prints the same `relations.blocks` and `relations.blockedBy` entries, by `edgeId`, that it printed at d0e4784.
5. Each entry that verb prints carries the same per-entry field names it carried at d0e4784.

11. That refusal names `forge knowledge list` and `forge knowledge get <slug>` as what still serves.
12. `forge knowledge write` with a `--kind` value outside the declared set refuses, naming the values it accepts.
13. `forge tools` prints one row per `(tool, action)` pair this CLI can serve, each carrying its HTTP method and path, with the `forge_uploads` and `forge_step_start` rows carrying `POST /mcp`.
14. `forge schema forge_issues` prints the arguments this CLI sends for each of that tool's actions, matching the route table's rows for that tool.
15. `forge schema forge_issues` sends no request to `/mcp`, judged on a capture of the requests that one invocation makes.
16. `forge call` naming a tool or action the route table has no row for exits non-zero.

18. `forge doctor` prints the MCP endpoint and the REST base, both derived from the one `url` value in the config file, for two different configured urls.
19. A `forge comment` write on ISS-508 posts the comment, and a subsequent `forge issue ISS-508 --full` read shows it.
20. `forge advance` moves ISS-508's status, and a subsequent read of ISS-508 shows the new status.

23. `plugin/test/tracker/rest.test.mjs` fails when any one projection that is not an identity is reverted to pass the REST body through unchanged.
24. `plugin/test/tracker/rest.test.mjs` asserts the projected shape for every row of the route table, identity rows included.
25. `npm run check` passes over the whole tree at the merged head.
26. The verdict for the walk names the wall time of one `forge next` run at d0e4784 and one at the merged head.
27. The installed plugin copy under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/forge-local/forge/<released version>/` answers `forge issue ISS-508` when invoked by its own path, with its requests captured and going to `/api`.

31. `forge tools` omits a tool recorded in the config file's `capabilities` as refusing this credential.
32. `forge tools --all` prints that same tool.

items.title: a project-config or project-detail call that fails at the transport takes down the advance it was made for
items.description:
## What happened

`stagingDeploy` and `releasePolicy` in `plugin/src/tracker/project-config.mjs` both reach the tracker
through `scoped(name, args, true)`. That third argument is `callTool`'s `soft`, which softens the
*tool's own refusal* and nothing else: `callTool`'s fourth argument, `transport`, defaults to false,
so an HTTP failure on either call goes down `rpc`'s hard path and exits the process.

Both are on `forge advance`'s path. `policyFor` awaits `releasePolicy` while building the view;
`refuseCredential` in `plugin/src/tracker/rpc.mjs` awaits `stagingDeploy` before every write, to
refuse a payload carrying the project's own test credential. So a tracker that answers
`forge_issues` and `forge_comments` and then fails on `forge_config` or `forge_projects.get` takes
down a rehearsal or a transition that had nothing to do with either reading.

Neither answer is load-bearing for the move being made. The release policy decides who is *asked*
to look; the deploy decides what a rehearsal *says* about a credential. A partial outage on those
two calls should cost the answer, not the command.

`tried` in the same module is the shape that already exists for this: it resolves the aim softly and
calls `callTool(name, args, true, true)`, handing back `{ refused }` instead of exiting.

## Outcome

A project-detail or project-config call that fails at the transport leaves the reading unanswered
and the command it was made for still able to finish.

## Rules

- An unanswered reading is `null` — the same value a project with no slug already yields — so every
  reader that already treats `null` as *not read* keeps its behaviour with no second state to learn.
- `refuseCredential` is the exception and stays hard, or gains a refusal of its own: it is the guard
  that stops a payload carrying a project's test credential, and a guard that passes what it could
  not check is worse than one that stops the command.
- The two readings answer alike. A rule that softened one and not the other would make which call
  failed decide whether a run survives.

## Where

`plugin/src/tracker/project-config.mjs` — `releasePolicy` and `stagingDeploy`, both `scoped(..., true)`.
`plugin/src/tracker/rpc.mjs` — `scoped`, `callTool`'s two flags, `tried` as the soft-transport shape,
and `refuseCredential`, which is the reader that must not go soft.

## Out of scope

`forge project` and `forge doctor`, whose whole subject is those readings: a command whose answer
*is* the project's configuration is right to fail when it cannot read it.

The advisory line at `tested` that reads the deploy, which is ISS-472's and reads `null` as silence
already.

## Why

Raised as F2 of the review consult on ISS-472 and accepted in part there: the half that was folded
narrowed the new reading to `--owed`, and this is the half that was rejected as neither that
change's to make nor safe to make at `refuseCredential`.
